title: When Validators and Repairs See the Same Candidate: A Confirmatory Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, paired experiment that evaluated a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The executed adapter used gpt-5-mini with retrieval disabled (retrieval_augmented_generation=false) and exactly one shared initial generation per task (generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate). On N=250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) judged every sampled initial candidate valid (250/250), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded final validity rates were identical (1.0). Mapping the preregistered estimand actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses were not testable because retrieval was disabled in the executed adapter; we document this preregistration deviation, quantify a power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈0.05 vs. observed actionable-misconfig rate 0.0), and discuss construct and external-validity limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, single deterministic validator, no RAG). All execution artifacts, preregistration, and analysis scripts are archived in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation, staged change planning, and zero-touch configuration. Because LLM outputs can violate ordering constraints or operational invariants, guarded architectures that combine generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) are widely advocated as a safety control. We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to test whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) can increase the rate of actionable misconfigurations. The run actually executed with generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation=false; consequently the executed estimand measures validator/repair effects on the identical single sampled candidate shared across baseline and guarded arms (baseline single-shot validity versus final guarded validity after permitted repair). We present the preregistered design, the concrete preregistration deviation (retrieval disabled), artifact-backed results, and an interpretation of what the executed evidence does—and does not—support.
sections.related_work: Surveys and application papers document active interest in applying LLMs to NetOps tasks including intent translation and automation; related work also proposes tool-augmented architectures that call deterministic validators or simulators to improve grounding. Prior studies and adjacent-domain adversarial work identify hallucination, constraint violations, and RAG-poisoning as reliability threats that motivate guarded pipelines and adversarial benchmarks. Existing empirical reports of validator augmentation show gains in limited settings but also note engineering and latency tradeoffs. Our study contributes a tightly preregistered, paired empirical probe of a guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics and provides artifact-backed accounting of a run where retrieval was disabled and the validator found no actionable faults.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract: The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1. The frozen execution contract actually run declared: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model=gpt-5-mini (provider openai_responses); generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate; retrieval_augmented_generation=false; initial_generation_calls_per_task=1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1; task_count=250; planned_episodes=500. The recorded model configuration set temperature=null/unset; explicitly, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the adapter reused exactly the same single sampled initial candidate for baseline and guarded arms; no independent per-condition sampling was performed. (A constrained-prompt arm in the preregistration was not executed as an independent generation condition.)

Tasks and validator: We used 250 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned a stored scorer label VALID_CONFIGURATION where stored 'success' = 1 indicates a valid, non-actionable configuration. To align preregistration and stored artifacts we operationalized the preregistered estimand actionable_misconfig as actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION (this mapping is applied consistently in analysis and reporting).

Experimental flow and analysis: For each task the adapter obtained a shared initial generation from the model (shared across conditions). Baseline recorded the validator result on that initial candidate. Guarded ran the deterministic validator and, if violations were reported, permitted at most one repair attempt; the final guarded result recorded the validator status after any permitted repair. The primary confirmatory test was a paired comparison of actionable_misconfig indicators (exact McNemar two-sided, α=0.05). We also computed paired bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 processed archived result files; all raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis code are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed as recorded (started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z; completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z). Planned episodes 500 (2×250) completed with zero failed episodes; provider-call audit recorded 250 hosted model call events corresponding to the shared initial generation stage. Representative artifacts (responses and validator traces) show identical shared initial candidates across baseline and guarded arms.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed): Using the stored scorer semantics (VALID_CONFIGURATION=1) and the mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION, the archived contingency table is n11=250, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (all 250 pairs had stored VALID_CONFIGURATION=1). Thus actionable-misconfig counts are all zero in both arms; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are archived and consistent with these numbers.

Preregistration deviation: The preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses (dose–response across poison fractions) required retrieval-augmented generation; the executed adapter had retrieval_augmented_generation=false and therefore injected no retrievals (clean or poisoned). This is a recorded, explicit deviation: the poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run and remain unexecuted.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation: Under the executed semantics—one shared initial sampled candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded, deterministic validator, and retrieval disabled—the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to change outcomes because every shared initial candidate passed validation. The narrow, artifact-backed conclusion is: when baseline and guarded arms begin from the same single valid candidate (per the deterministic validator used here), the guarded pipeline produced no paired change in actionable misconfiguration rate. This should not be generalized to assert guarded pipelines lack utility: (1) a guarded pipeline's marginal benefit depends on the base rate of invalid initial candidates under a chosen model/prompt; (2) shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate validator/repair effects but prevent measurement of independent generation variability across arms; (3) disabling retrievals means RAG-poisoning hypotheses were not tested.

Power and assumption mismatch: The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈0.05 and targeted detection of an absolute paired increase ≈0.05 with 80% power. The observed baseline actionable-misconfig rate was 0.0, violating that assumption and invalidating the preregistered sensitivity interpretation for the original poisoning hypothesis. Consequently the observed zero-event outcome does not constitute a sensitive test of RAG-poisoning.

Threats to validity: Internal validity — shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced and archived; this design isolates validator/repair effects but precludes measuring independent-generation variability. Construct validity — the deterministic validator implements rule-based checks and may omit production failure modes (vendor-specific semantics, asynchronous state). External validity — synthetic task families, single LLM (gpt-5-mini), single deterministic validator, and disabled retrieval limit generalization to heterogeneous production topologies and to RAG-enabled threat models. Conclusion validity — the exact zero-event outcome yields precise bootstrapped CIs here, but that precision reflects homogeneous outcomes in this controlled corpus rather than broad operational safety.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The execution (gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator; retrieval disabled) produced 250/250 VALID_CONFIGURATION outcomes, no repairs were applied, and no actionable misconfigurations were observed in either arm (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Crucially, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable because retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter; this preregistration deviation and a power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈0.05 vs. observed 0.0) limit confirmatory inference about retrieval-poisoning. Follow-up experiments that enable controlled retrieval augmentation and poisoning injection, broaden validator realism, and evaluate independent-generation semantics are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with a single sampled initial generation per task; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as a preregistration deviation.

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping is applied consistently in all reported analyses.

Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
